title: What are the main types of CCTV cameras?

scenes.title: CCTV: Eyes Everywhere
scenes.narration: CCTV, or Closed-Circuit Television, uses cameras to transmit video to a limited set of monitors, creating a private surveillance network. This system helps deter crime and provides crucial evidence, with over 1 billion cameras globally.

scenes.title: The Signal Journey
scenes.narration: A CCTV system functions like a digital nervous system, where the camera acts as the eye, capturing visual data. This data is then converted into an electrical signal and transmitted, much like a message sent through a secure channel.

scenes.title: Core Components
scenes.narration: A complete CCTV setup involves a camera for image capture, a Digital Video Recorder (DVR) or Network Video Recorder (NVR) for processing and storage, and a monitor for live viewing. Network cables or Wi-Fi connect these elements.

scenes.title: Smart Surveillance
scenes.narration: Modern CCTV systems integrate AI and analytics for advanced features like facial recognition and motion detection. This transforms passive monitoring into proactive security, alerting users to specific events rather than constant manual review.

scenes.title: Impact and Future
scenes.narration: CCTV systems are vital for public safety, asset protection, and operational efficiency across various sectors. The future promises more integrated, intelligent, and energy-efficient systems, further enhancing security capabilities.
